paper.title: Combined Biological and Numerical Modeling Approach for Better Understanding of the Cancer Viability and Apoptosis
paper.displayTitle: Combined biological and numerical modeling of cancer viability and apoptosis
paper.authorsShort: Marko Živanović, M. Gazdić Janković, A. Ramović Hamzagić, K. Virijević, N. Milivojević, … B. Ljujić, N. Filipović

question: When clinical chemotherapeutics hit cancer and healthy cells, how do the cells die, and can a growth–death model capture the whole time course?

mainFinding.label: as reported
mainFinding.text: All eight drugs lowered viability in a dose- and time-dependent way, mostly through late apoptosis along the intrinsic pathway. A growth–death model fitted per condition reproduces the viability curves.

fits.rtcaB: RTCA values at flow time points

methods.title: Cell lines and treatment
paragraphs: HCT-116 (colorectal carcinoma), MDA-MB-231 (breast adenocarcinoma) and MRC-5 (lung fibroblast, healthy reference), all from ECACC, grown in DMEM with 10% FBS at 37 °C, 5% CO₂.

Colorectal regimen drugs (5-FU, leucovorin, irinotecan, oxaliplatin) on HCT-116 and MRC-5; breast regimen drugs (doxorubicin, endoxan, paclitaxel, docetaxel) on MDA-MB-231 and MRC-5. Flow cytometry and qPCR used two doses per drug; RTCA used up to five.

methods.title: Real-time viability (RTCA)
paragraphs: xCELLigence RTCA DP, E-plate 16, 10,000 cells per well, impedance read every 15 min for 96 h. Chemotherapeutics were added about 24 h after seeding; results are expressed as normalized cell index (NCI).
notes: Curves are shown as in Supplementary Figs. S1–S4: time since seeding, resampled to 1 h. The dashed vertical line marks drug addition. Error bars are shown at selected time points, as in the Supplementary, so the curves stay readable.

methods.title: Cell death type (Annexin V / PI flow cytometry)
paragraphs: 2 × 10⁵ cells per sample, BD FACSVerse, 24 h and 72 h after treatment. Viable: Annexin V⁻ PI⁻. Early apoptosis: Annexin V⁺ PI⁻. Late apoptosis: Annexin V⁺ PI⁺. Necrosis: Annexin V⁻ PI⁺. Means of three independent experiments.

methods.title: Apoptosis genes (qPCR)
paragraphs: TRIzol RNA, oligo(dT) cDNA, qPCR against β-actin. Targets Bcl-2, Bax, Cas3 (caspase 3), Cas9 (caspase 9) and Fas. Relative expression by 2^−ΔΔCt [ref:24], reported as fold change against untreated cells. No error estimates are given in Fig. S9.

methods.title: Numerical model and fitting
paragraphs: Two-phase avascular tumour model [ref:25], cell migration switched off. α is the cell fraction, C the oxygen concentration, held constant outside the cells.
notes: FEM in 2D (in-house), 1 h step, 72 h. Q and Q₁ were fitted on controls only (HCT-116 5.32 / 4.97; MDA-MB-231 5.31 / 4.29; MRC-5 4.69 / 3.98). s₁–s₄ were fitted per condition to viable-cell percentages at 24, 36, 48, 60 and 72 h by SQP followed by Nelder–Mead [ref:29], first to RTCA alone, then to RTCA and flow together.
The logistic fit shown in chapter 4 is a separate re-analysis made for this page, not the paper's model.

methods.title: Statistics
paragraphs: Three independent experiments, at least three replicates each. Mean ± SD (RTCA) or ± SEM (flow). Mann–Whitney test and one-way ANOVA.

limitations.title: Monolayers in a dish
limitations.text: 2D cultures in normoxia, one cell line per tumour type, as stated in the paper.

limitations.title: RTCA measures adhesion
limitations.text: Impedance reflects attached cells; flow cytometry is needed to tell how cells die.

limitations.title: Transcripts, not proteins
limitations.text: Pathway activity is inferred from mRNA levels of five genes.

limitations.title: Model scope
limitations.text: Parameters are fitted per condition; predicting other concentrations is named in the paper as the next step.

text: In the treatment of HCT-116 cells with 5-FU, we obtained a significant response from the treated cells in terms of a decrease in cell viability in a dose-dependent manner.
Perhaps the most significant result was obtained with the use of oxaliplatin, where an exceptional result of selectivity towards HCT-116 cells was obtained.
In HCT-116 cells, all 4 applied drugs show a significant effect, especially in the form of induction of late apoptosis in the treatments.
In MDA-MB-231 cells, all four selected drugs show a similar effect: an increase in the proportion of late apoptosis and necrosis with an increase in the dose and time of exposure.
In HCT-116 cells (Figure S9) Bcl and Bax genes show increased expression indicating that these drugs induce apoptosis in a dose- and time-dependent manner.

The results on all three cell lines indicate a dominant reduction or slight fluctuation of Fas gene expression, which indicates that the extrinsic apoptosis pathway is not favored in these treatments.
As can be concluded from the sensitivity analysis, smaller values of parameters s2 and s3 and higher values of parameter s4 indicate that the cytotoxicity of the applied chemotherapeutic is higher.

The next step in the process of future improvements of the presented model will be to use the values of estimated parameters for considered concentrations of pharmacological treatments as a basis to predict the values of parameters for other concentrations.
